sentences.text: The Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies distribution circuits through transformer and feeder bays.
The station automation boundary covers bay-level monitoring and control, station coordination, and the interfaces to external operating personnel and systems.
Primary equipment, protection functions, and field wiring remain subject to their approved designs and operating limits.
The Bay Automation Controller is assigned the project codename Juniper.
The Bay Automation Controller performs bay-level sequencing, status evaluation, and control permissive checks.
The Bay Automation Controller produces a Bay Status Digest for operational awareness.
North Bay Controller and South Bay Controller provide bay-specific automation for their respective portions of the station.
The Feeder Protection Relay detects feeder faults and initiates protection actions within its configured protection zone.
The Feeder Protection Relay produces a Relay Diagnostic Note when its self-monitoring identifies a condition requiring engineering attention.
Protection trips remain independent of routine bay-control commands so that a control-system failure does not inhibit fault clearing.
The Breaker Control Unit executes authorized breaker operations and enforces its local electrical and mechanical interlocks.
The Bay Automation Controller requests breaker operations only when the applicable operating mode and permissives allow them.
Local control takes precedence when equipment is selected for local operation.
Remote commands are subject to station authority, bay selection, interlocking, and equipment availability.
The Station Supervisory Control System provides the station-level operating interface and supervisory coordination.
The Station Gateway defines the communications boundary for authorized connections beyond the station automation network.
The Satellite Time Receiver provides the station with a reference for time synchronization.
The Sequence Event Archive retains operational event information for later review.
The Engineering Workstation supports authorized configuration and maintenance activities under controlled access.
The Maintenance Remote Terminal is limited to approved maintenance access and does not replace local operating authority.
The Station DC System supplies control power to automation and protection equipment within its design capacity.
The Control Room Operator directs routine station operation and verifies that commanded equipment states are appropriate.
The Protection Relay Engineer maintains protection settings and evaluates relay performance within the approved change process.
The Substation Field Crew performs field checks and equipment work under the applicable switching instructions and clearances.
